milestone.title: Watch state-machine correctness across mp and Raul

intent.outcome: Watch follows one delivery lifecycle (complete means delivery done; review cycle in reviews registry); live run state persists on every observable transition; Raul preflight binds to an exact queue fingerprint; idle polling advances without keypresses.

problem.description: Watch prompts and the state machine disagree on self-reviewed/reviewed. Live state is often only persisted at start/end. Per-item skip can mark the whole run terminal. Raul can start a queue different from the preflighted one. Crossterm wait_next blocks so the 3s poller only runs after input.

in_scope: Align prompts, next-stage, and eligibility with Option A delivery lifecycle
WatchRunStore::transition for atomic live persistence (observed lifecycle snapshot only)
Preflight fingerprint + invalidation on every queue mutation
Deadline-aware EventSource idle ticks; Watch restoration on lane init
Export eligibility projection; remove Raul allowlist drift
out_of_scope: Typed milestone transition table implementation details beyond consuming Group C

design_decisions.choice: Keep delivery phases small: complete means delivery completed; self/external review-cycle lives solely in the reviews registry; treat self-reviewed and reviewed as legacy read/migration aliases, not active Watch destinations (Option A).
design_decisions.rationale: Watch prompts already teach Option A while state_machine.rs still waits on self-reviewed/reviewed, producing a contradictory second lifecycle (Finding 15).

design_decisions.choice: Introduce WatchRunStore::transition(event) that atomically persists stage, role, target, pane IDs, observed lifecycle snapshot, and per-item outcome; it never performs milestone lifecycle transitions (those go through mp durable executor).
design_decisions.rationale: Live Watch state is only persisted at run start/end today, so control/status readers miss mid-run stage (Finding 16).

design_decisions.choice: Keep per-item outcomes separate from aggregate run outcome; the sequencer is the sole owner of terminal run classification and emits PartialFailure for mixed completed/skipped/failed queues after halt or exhaustion.
design_decisions.rationale: Per-item skip currently marks the entire Watch run terminal while later items remain active (Finding 17).

design_decisions.choice: Successful preflight stores the exact ordered queue fingerprint; every queue mutation path invalidates preflight and can_start compares current vs preflight fingerprint; restored queues always require a fresh matching preflight.
design_decisions.rationale: Preflight remains valid after add/remove/reorder so Raul can start a different queue than the one that was preflighted (Finding 5 / 18).

design_decisions.choice: EventSource waits until input arrives or the next Watch poll deadline expires; CrosstermSource uses event::poll(timeout) then read; timeout is an idle tick (not EOS); preserve burst coalescing and frame-rate limiting.
design_decisions.rationale: wait_next blocks indefinitely so the 3s Watch poller only runs after a keypress (Finding 6).

design_decisions.choice: Route Watch mutations through App methods or mutation results that call app.touch() exactly when state changes; cover selection, cursors, preflight, start/stop, refresh, clear, status, output, and errors.
design_decisions.rationale: Several Watch actions mutate state without bumping App::version so the view never redraws (Additional Watch redraw remediation).

steps.action: Introduce WatchRunStore::transition(event) that atomically persists stage, role, target, pane IDs, observed lifecycle snapshot, and per-item outcome on every externally observable transition; protect with short-lived lock or generation/CAS; preserve last valid snapshot on transient I/O failure; never perform milestone lifecycle transitions.

steps.done_when: Control/status readers observe active milestone and stage mid-run; every transition increments generation and is atomically readable; concurrent stop/status do not overwrite newer snapshots.

steps.action: Keep per-item outcomes separate from aggregate run outcome; make the sequencer the sole owner of terminal classification; compute one aggregate after halt or queue exhaustion; retain and emit PartialFailure for any mixture of completed/skipped/failed item outcomes.
steps.tests: cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_dry_run --test watch_control --no-fail-fast
steps.done_when: Skip followed by another milestone remains non-terminal; mixed queue produces documented aggregate; classification never reports terminal while a later item is active.

steps.action: Invoke Watch restoration when the Watch lane initializes; restore persisted queue and terminal outcome together after candidates load; reconcile missing candidates by stable ID and surface omissions; require a new preflight before restarting a restored queue.
steps.done_when: Restart after completed/stopped/failed/partial restores matching queue; missing IDs handled deterministically; start disabled until fresh matching preflight.

steps.action: Represent successful preflight with exact ordered queue fingerprint; centralize queue mutations to update selection/cursors, clear candidate dependency status where required, invalidate preflight, and mark dirty; can_start compares current vs preflight fingerprint; invalidate on toggle/set/clear/reorder/refresh/dependency changes.
steps.done_when: Preflight+add/remove/reorder/clear invalidates; same-queue refresh preserves; failed preflight never enables start; restored selections require new preflight.

steps.action: Change EventSource to wait until input arrives or next idle/poll deadline; implement CrosstermSource with event::poll(timeout)+read; timeout is idle tick not EOS; calculate timeout from Watch poller next deadline; preserve burst coalescing and frame-rate limiting.
steps.done_when: Fake time with no input yields repeated on_idle; Watch redraws after status changes without keypress; no busy loop before deadline; queued input remains responsive.

steps.action: Expose Watch changes through App methods or mutation results that the action dispatcher converts into app.touch(); cover selection, both cursors, preflight, start, stop, refresh, clear, status, output, and errors; avoid unconditional redraws when no state changed.
steps.done_when: Each Watch action bumps version exactly when state changes; event loop renders the changed view; clippy clean.

findings.description: Finding 16 residual (L1/L2): `cmd_watch_control_stop` checks `run_outcome.is_none()` on a pre-lock load, then calls `WatchRunStore::transition(RunOutcome::GracefullyStopped)`. `transition` reloads under the lock and `set_run_outcome` always overwrites — there is no terminal-outcome guard. Race: (1) stop loads with run_outcome=None, (2) driver persists Completed/PartialFailure, (3) stop's transition reloads the newer terminal snapshot and replaces it with gracefully-stopped. This violates Finding 16's "concurrent stop/status updates do not overwrite newer snapshots" contract. Fix: inside `transition`/`set_run_outcome` (or the stop caller under the lock), refuse RunOutcome writes when an outcome is already present; add a regression that interleaves Completed then stop's GracefullyStopped and asserts Completed survives.
findings.author: coordinator-stage8
findings.summary: watch-control stop can overwrite a newer terminal run_outcome

findings.description: Finding 18 residual: `restore_queue_from_status` normalizes persisted queue ids with `trim_start_matches('M')` so they match Raul candidates, but `parse_status` keeps `milestone_outcomes[].id` verbatim from the state file. `render_compact_queue` matches selected ids to outcome ids with exact string equality. If the watch queue was started with M-prefixed CLI ids (e.g. `mp watch M02`), restore yields selected=["02"] while outcomes still carry id="M02", so the restored terminal queue renders as pending instead of the recorded kinds. Repro shape is already in `restoring_terminal_queue_requires_new_preflight_and_reports_missing_ids` (queue uses M02/M01). Fix: normalize outcome ids the same way as queue ids (or compare via `normalize_milestone_id`), and pin a restore+render regression.
findings.author: coordinator-stage8
findings.summary: Restore strips M-prefix from queue but not outcome IDs
